{{Short description|American mathematician}}

[[File:KlausSchmittPortrait.png|thumb|Portrait of Professor Klaus Schmitt]]

'''Klaus Schmitt''' (May 1940, [[Rimbach, Hesse|Rimbach/Odenwald]] – April 2025 [[Mesquite, Nevada]])<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=December 2025 |title=Remembering Klaus Schmitt |url=https://www.math.utah.edu/about/news/remembering-klaus-schmitt.php |access-date=2026-06-23 |website=Department of Mathematics - The University of Utah}}</ref> was an American [[mathematician]] doing research in [[non-linear differential equations|nonlinear differential equations]], and [[nonlinear analysis]].

Schmitt completed the [[Abitur]] at Rimbach's Martin-Luther-Schule in 1960. He received a BA in mathematics and physics from [[St. Olaf College]] in 1962, an MA (1964) and PhD in mathematics from the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln|University of Nebraska]] in 1967. He began his 43-year career at the [[University of Utah]] in 1967, first as assistant, then associate, then as full professor of mathematics. He also served as chairman of the department of mathematics from 1989 to 1992.

Schmitt served short-term appointments as visiting professor at the [[University of Würzburg]], [[University of Karlsruhe]], [[University of Stuttgart]], [[Université catholique de Louvain|University Catholique de Louvain]], [[University of Bremen]], [[Technische Universität Berlin]], [[University of Heidelberg]], [[University of Kaiserslautern]], [[University of Sydney]], [[University of Chile|Universidad de Chile]], [[Universidad Catolica de Chile]], [[National Chengchi University]] in Taiwan, [[National Tsing Hua University]] in Taiwan and the [[Chern Institute of Mathematics]] in Tianjin, China.

He retired from the University of Utah as professor emeritus of mathematics in 2010.<ref name=":0" />

Schmitt was awarded the [[Humboldt Prize]] in mathematics in 1978 and was honored as a University of Nebraska Distinguished Alumnus in 2000.
